summary: One concrete instance of the Wave 33 'out-of-band DDL' class survives the corrected replay, and it needs a yes/no from the domain that owns the column before the next CP-016 regeneration. public.scheduled_posts.platform_status and .platform_errors are added by 20250904110000, which runs BEFORE 20260413200000 creates the table, inside an `alter table if exists` guard. A fresh chain replay therefore never creates them, while the generated contract does not declare them either, so the two currently agree. If any live target received scheduled_posts before 20250904110000 ran, that target has the columns and a regeneration would silently drop them from lib/database.types.ts.
completed: Located the cause: migration version order is not calendar order. 20250904110000 (2025-09-04) sorts before 20260413200000 (2026-04-13), so the ALTER precedes the CREATE in any replay that applies the chain in version order.

Confirmed the ALTER is guarded (`alter table if exists` plus a to_regclass check in the enclosing DO block), so a fresh replay skips it silently rather than aborting. The replay records this as skippedRelationAbsentAtReplay, not as a chain abort.

Confirmed the contract is silent on both columns, so the superset property the CP-016 gate depends on currently holds for them. `node supabase/tests/db008_chain_contract_replay.mjs . <out> --check` exits 0.

Found the same shape in five more ALTERs, all guarded and all harmless: 20250813121000 alters public.staff_invitations four times before 20250813123000 creates it, but the later CREATE declares tour_id, role, origin and created_by in its own body, so the columns do arrive. Only the scheduled_posts pair is genuinely lost.

RESOLVED, not answered with a yes/no. Measured instead: a fresh replay really does skip the two columns (reproduced in supabase/tests/db008_scheduled_posts_platform.harness.sh from the two real chain files), AND the columns are NOT dead - app/api/artist/content/overview/route.ts:137 selects them and lib/services/cross-platform-posting.service.ts:195 writes one. The correct outcome was therefore neither branch of the original question: the columns are live, the chain is wrong, and 20260926140200_scheduled_posts_platform_columns.sql repairs it forward. The contract still declares neither, which is now explicitly recorded as CP-016 debt rather than as safety.
next_steps: Answer one question: does any live environment have public.scheduled_posts.platform_status or .platform_errors? Read-only probe: `select column_name from information_schema.columns where table_schema='public' and table_name='scheduled_posts' and column_name in ('platform_status','platform_errors');` on staging and on production.

If NO target has them, the columns are dead: 20250904110000 was written against a table that did not exist yet and never took effect anywhere. Record that and no migration is needed. Do not capture them.

If ANY target has them, they are genuine out-of-band DDL and must be captured as an additive migration so the chain stays a superset of the contract. Say which target and I will author it; I will not guess the nullability or default from the guarded ALTER alone.

Separately, and yours to decide: 20250904110000 is a migration that cannot do what it says on a fresh target. Whether to repair it forward (an additive migration that adds the columns unconditionally) or to retire it is a social-domain call about whether the per-platform status tracking is still a feature.
blockers: The regeneration precondition currently holds, so this is not blocking today. It becomes blocking the moment a target is found that has the columns: at that point regeneration would delete real coverage, which is the exact Wave 33 blocker and the reason that finding had to be retracted on measurement rather than trusted.
The probe requires target credentials the database lane does not have. No hosted read was performed and none is claimed.
verification: node supabase/tests/db008_chain_contract_replay.mjs . <out> --report prints: `ALTERs a fresh replay would skip ... 6` and names 20250904110000 as skippedRelationAbsentAtReplay with `columns a fresh replay never creates: platform_status, platform_errors`.

The harness assertion `a genuinely skipped column is absent from chain and contract alike` in supabase/tests/db008_contract_reproducibility.harness.sh pins the current agreement, so a future chain edit that makes the two disagree fails the gate instead of passing quietly.
